red_flags: Fever with hypotension, mottling, or confusion (sepsis)
Fever with neck stiffness, photophobia, or new rash
Fever with bleeding (gums, nose, GI) after animal/tick contact — CCHF until proven otherwise: isolate and notify
Fever with severe localised bone or spine pain and inability to walk
Fever > 2 weeks with weight loss and night sweats
Fever in a patient with a prosthetic valve or new murmur
Neutropenia risk: fever on chemotherapy or known low white count
exam: Record full vitals: temperature, BP, pulse, respiratory rate, SpO2 — relative bradycardia with high fever suggests typhoid
Assess mentation and neck stiffness; test Kernig's sign if meningitis is possible
Inspect skin fully: rose spots on trunk (typhoid), petechiae or ecchymoses (CCHF, meningococcaemia), splinter haemorrhages (endocarditis)
Auscultate the heart for a new or changed murmur (endocarditis)
Auscultate lungs for focal crackles or bronchial breathing (pneumonia)
Palpate the abdomen for splenomegaly (typhoid, brucellosis, endocarditis) and hepatomegaly
Percuss the renal angles for tenderness (pyelonephritis)
Press over the lumbar spine and sacroiliac joints — focal tenderness raises brucellar spondylitis
Palpate all lymph node regions for enlarged nodes (TB, viral syndromes)
Examine large joints for swelling or effusion (brucellar arthritis)
Inspect the throat and ears to close out simple upper respiratory sources

investigations.why: Neutrophilia supports pyogenic infection (pneumonia, pyelonephritis); leukopenia with relative lymphocytosis supports typhoid or viral illness; thrombocytopenia + leukopenia after animal exposure raises CCHF; pancytopenia raises visceral leishmaniasis or marrow disease

investigations.test: Blood culture (two sets, before any antibiotic)
investigations.why: Rules in typhoid (first week), brucellosis (prolonged incubation — tell the lab), and endocarditis; the yield collapses after antibiotics start, so draw first
Pyuria and nitrites with a positive culture rule in urinary tract infection/pyelonephritis and close the search; a clean urine removes it from the list

investigations.test: Brucella serology (standard agglutination test / Rose Bengal)
investigations.why: Rules brucellosis in or out in undulant fever with raw-milk or livestock exposure, back pain, or arthritis — a leading cause of prolonged fever in Iraq
Tracks inflammatory burden; very high ESR supports endocarditis, TB, or deep abscess over simple viral illness; near-normal values argue against serious bacterial disease
Rules in pneumonia and screens for TB (upper-zone disease, cavitation, hilar nodes) when the fever has no source on exam

investigations.test: Malaria film / rapid test AND typhoid-directed serology only if culture unavailable
investigations.why: Blood film if travel to an endemic area (rare within Iraq); Widal is unreliable alone — interpret only with the clinical picture when culture is not possible
Confirms splenomegaly/hepatomegaly (typhoid, brucellosis, leishmaniasis), finds liver abscess or renal obstruction with pyelonephritis when fever stays unexplained
If new murmur, positive blood cultures, or persistent unexplained fever with valve risk — vegetations rule endocarditis in
